# Epistle of Barnabas Chapter 16 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET / LOGOS / PNEUMA

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: "wretched people" vs. "poor, misguided people"
- EMET: "wretched people"
- LOGOS: "wretched people"
- PNEUMA: "poor, misguided people"
- **Ruling:** "wretched people" — *talaiporoi anthrōpoi* — *talaipouria* = wretchedness/misery; "wretched" has the right tone of pity mixed with condemnation; PNEUMA softens this too much.

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: "span" vs. "palm of the hand"
- EMET: "measured the heaven with his span"
- LOGOS: "measured the heaven with a span"
- PNEUMA: "measured out the sky with the palm of his hand"
- **Ruling:** "measured the heaven with a span" — *drakti* = a span (width of outstretched hand); "span" is the technical term for this unit of measure; "palm" (PNEUMA) is inaccurate for this particular word.

## Disagreement 3 — v.6: "when the week is completed" vs. "when the week is ended"
- EMET: "when the week is completed"
- LOGOS: "when the week is ended"
- PNEUMA: "when the week comes to an end"
- **Ruling:** "when the week is ended" — *syntelesthēnai tēn hebdomada* — both "ended" and "completed" capture *sunteleō*; "ended" is slightly more natural in English; all three are acceptable.

## Disagreement 4 — v.9: "door of the temple, which is the mouth" — handling the allegory
- EMET: "opening... the door of the temple, which is the mouth"
- LOGOS: "opening... the door of the temple, which is the mouth"
- PNEUMA: "He opened for us... the door of the temple — which is the mouth"
- **Ruling:** Retain "which is the mouth" — the appositive gloss is in the text; do not move it to a footnote. All agents agree; LOGOS structure is clearest.

## Disagreement 5 — v.10: "marveling" vs. "being amazed"
- EMET: "being amazed that he never... heard these words"
- LOGOS: "marveling that they never before heard these words"
- PNEUMA: "marveling that these words were never heard before"
- **Ruling:** "marveling that they never before heard these words" — LOGOS; *thaumazonta* = marveling/wondering; "marveling" is more precise than "being amazed" (EMET); PNEUMA changes the subject from "they" to an impersonal "these words were never heard," losing the personal experience.

**Total disagreements: 5**
